routing_policy._note: HV-7 (owner-signed 2026-07-21), derived from the HV-6b in-segment grid. AUTO-ACCEPT iff the rule engine and the AI voter AGREE on the same non-blank category AND ai_confidence >= min_ai_confidence AND that category is not in demoted_categories. Everything else routes to review with a BLANK final_category_id (votes are persisted but never surfaced -- a blank final is route-to-human, never a category). PRIORITY within review: ai_confidence < priority_max_ai_confidence OR both voters blank. MEASURED on the combined 2,354-row corpus: auto-accept 70.4% at 98.67% (Set-2 67.8% at 98.53%), review share 29.6%, 22 wrong rows auto-accepted. THE DEMOTION LIST IS DATA, NOT CODE -- it is re-derived from the in-segment grid at every evaluation cycle (it already moved once: v4.0's {Cables, Ducting, Sensors} became v4.1's {AHU, Cables, Sensors} when the HV-6b surface change fixed Ducting and exposed AHU). Never hard-code it in routing.py. OPT-IN per discipline: rules_electrical.json carries no routing_policy block and keeps the legacy R3d path byte-identically. Set-1 and Set-2 are both spent, so these values are OWED a confirmation on production Set-3.

_matching_surface_note: HV-6b (2026-07-21, OWNER GATE WAIVER): HVAC matches rules against a TWO-PASS surface. Pass 1 is NOTES-FREE -- item/exclusion rules see the row description only, ancestor rules see ancestor descriptions only, each at its own level. Pass 2 runs the LEGACY full surface (descriptions + all notes, own and ancestor) ONLY when pass 1 abstains outright. A pass-1 verdict wins as-is. OPT-IN per discipline: rules_electrical.json carries no key and runs the legacy single pass byte-identically (proven: 1,384 corpus line items, 0 differ, identical verdict hash). MEASURED: the notes in this corpus are specification boilerplate averaging ~700 characters, and token-matching over them cost the rule engine 161 net rows via false matches while rescuing 32 bare-fragment rows whose own description names no item -- consulting notes only on abstain keeps both. Combined 2,354-row corpus: 68.39% -> 75.49%; Set-2 64.13% -> 73.07%; agreement with AI v1.2 69.80% -> 77.74%; review share 37.6% -> 29.6% at 98.67% auto-accept accuracy. The owner WAIVED the probe's per-category gate (ADP -6 correct rows against a <=5 threshold) on 2026-07-21, accepting the trade: ADP precision 67.4% -> 82.6% on the corpus's largest category (627 rows) plus +161 net rows overall. THE AI FEED IS UNTOUCHED -- the voter still reads notes in full, because it reads them semantically rather than by token. Set-1 and Set-2 are both spent, so this must be CONFIRMED on production Set-3 before the routing policy is re-cut against it. Evidence: _classification_review/hvac_notes_probe/NOTES_PROBE.md + hvac_v41_acceptance/ACCEPTANCE_V41.md.
final_rulings: HV-6 (2026-07-21) encodes the owner's THREE FINAL rulings as rule law, each carrying source 'owner ruling 2026-07-21'. (1) CHW/DX BOUNDARY -- the FEED MEDIUM decides, never the form factor: water-fed -> hvac_chw_units, refrigerant-fed -> hvac_dx_unit, and cassette/hi-wall/ductable/split are FORM words that resolve only together with a context signal from the line's own text OR its section header (CHW-CASSETTE/DX-CASSETTE re-stated, CHW-ANC widened with water-fed/water-cooled, new DX-ANC mirroring CHW-ANC at 0.4). Bare form with NEITHER context stays weak and contested on purpose -- do not guess. VRF keeps precedence because VRF is refrigerant-fed too (new ancestor-scoped DX-VRF-EXCL); the bare word 'refrigerant' is deliberately NOT a DX-ANC token, since measuring it cost 4 VRF rows. (2) VRF CONTROLLERS -- a VRF/VRV system's OWN controls (corded/wireless remote, centralised remote controller, intelligent touch manager) price with the VRF package (new VRF-CONTROLS at 0.55), guarded the other way so Sensors keeps the BMS basket only (new SNS-VRFCTRL-EXCL). (3) MISC -- owner ruling: UNCHANGED, deliberately. PNL-ANC-TYPE was NOT modified: both implementable fixes measured WORSE on the combined 2,354-row corpus (delete -0.98 pp / 23 rows broken; headers_only -0.21 pp / 5 broken) because the rule correctly resolves bare fragment leaves such as 'For 15HP' under a panel header. Its Set-2 defect is real but the in-scope remedies cost more than they save -- see _classification_review/hvac_rules_v4_verify/VERIFY_V4.md. MEASURED RULES-ONLY: 68.22% -> 68.39% on the combined corpus; prompt v1.3's parallel edits are measured at the HV-7 certification run.
boundary_register: HV-5 (2026-07-21) encodes the owner's Boundary Rulings register as rule law. R1 flexible/foil duct -> ADP (Ducting is rigid fabricated sheet-metal only). R2 pipeline instruments (BTU/energy/flow meter, thermometer, gauges, test points, thermowells) -> Valve Package at full weight; Sensors keeps the BMS basket only. R3 plenum -> ADP, beating an AHU section. R4 starter/control/VFD panel -> Panels, beating an AHU section. R5 damper accessories (actuators, fire sensors, MFD/damper control panels) -> ADP in damper context only. R6 canvas/flexible connections resolve by SERVED context: fan section -> Fans, duct/ADP section -> ADP. R7 filters integral to a unit -> that unit; standalone filter items -> Misc. R8 air curtains -> Misc. R9 an FCU quoted with a factory-fitted valve package stays CHW Units. R10 work/service lines (recommissioning, tapping, dismantling, modification) -> Misc regardless of the system they touch, guarded so a supply+install scope still wins. Each rule carries its provenance in `source`. MEASURED RULES-ONLY this slice; the parallel prompt v1.2 edits are measured at the next AI run.
note: HVAC category ruleset v2 (Build slice HV-4, 2026-07-20). v2 = v1 + the nearest-hit ancestor resolution flag (see ancestor_resolution) + TWO label-mined ancestor rules, each clearing the declared mining floor (support >= 8 truth rows, >= 2 distinct BoQs, precision >= 85%) with its figures recorded in its own source string: VLV-ANC-TYPE (support=136/boqs=5/prec=86.1) and FAN-ANC-TYPE (support=76/boqs=6/prec=96.2). Set-1 rules accuracy 52.86% -> 66.91% on the same 1,366 rows. MINED ON PROVISIONAL LABELS -- a re-mine is OWED at clean labels, and the 5x gain:loss keep-rule that governed the batch loop applies fresh at that re-mine. Batches that measured negative (duct / ADP / insulation / BMS ancestor vocabulary) and one that measured net-positive but traded badly (ADP, +3 rows for ~30 lost) were REJECTED and are recorded in the rescore report for retry at clean labels. NO weight changes were made to any v1 rule. Original HV-3 note follows. HVAC category ruleset v1 (Build slice HV-3, 2026-07-20). v1 changes are EVIDENCE-DRIVEN from the Set-1 label scoring (_classification_review/hvac_labels_and_scoring/SCORING_V0.md, 1366 scored line items) and each carries source 'set1-scoring 2026-07-20 (provisional labels)'. FOUR changes only: (a) RACEWAY CARVE-OUT -- new hvac_raceway category owns cable tray / raceway vocabulary, removed from Cables, with a false-friend guard each way; (b) H4 CONFIRMED (100%, n=66) -- an insulation word that is an ATTRIBUTE of a pipe/valve line no longer claims the row (the owner's 4A ruling); (c) H2 REVERSED -- the air-distribution ancestor was RIGHT 84% of the time, so the token is KEPT rather than dropped, but ADP-ANC's weight STAYS AT 0.4 (raising it to 0.45/0.5 was measured at 52.86% -> 50.29% and owner-REJECTED; this note previously said 'RAISED 0.4 -> 0.5', which never shipped -- corrected at HV-4); (d) H1 + H7 REFUTED -- their proposed edits are NOT applied; a WEAK provisional BTU/energy-meter -> Valve Package rule is added instead. H3/H5/H6 came back MIXED and are deliberately UNTOUCHED -- proximity decay reshuffles those piles and they re-arbitrate at clean labels. The top-level 'decay' block is the HVAC proximity-decay curve, PROVISIONAL-FIT (see its own note). Original HV-1 note follows. HVAC category ruleset v0 (Build slice HV-1). Mirrors the electrical rule grammar EXACTLY (rule_id, category_id, signal_type item_keyword/ancestor/exclusion, match, match_mode, weight, plain, source). Weights follow electrical conventions: a strong distinctive keyword 0.55-0.6, a supporting/ambiguous keyword 0.30-0.45, an ancestor section header 0.40-0.45; item_keyword matches description+notes, ancestor matches the parent_node ancestor chain. UNMEASURED v0 seeded from the HVAC corpus recon + pricing catalogue; weights are provisional and tunable via scoring.json (shared with electrical). COLLISION OWNERS: ADP owns dampers (incl. fire dampers); Cables owns ALL HVAC cabling incl. VRF control cabling (VRF keeps only refnet/gas/stand ancillaries); cassette/hi-wall/TR is ambiguous CHW-vs-DX-vs-VRF and is scored WEAK so it lands LOW/MED (never false-HIGH) unless a chilled-water/split/VRF context resolves it; Panels excludes double-skin/plenum casing (that is AHU/ADP); Pumps + Piping exclude drain-pump/drip-tray (that belongs to the unit).
_ancestor_resolution_note: HV-4: HVAC resolves ancestor signals at the NEAREST ancestor that fires anything, instead of flattening the whole chain into one blob. Only signals at that resolution point contribute; farther ancestors contribute nothing. This also switches HVAC onto the deterministic tie-break chain (score -> rule weight -> distinct signal types -> declaration order) instead of the legacy alphabetical-by-category_id tiebreak. OPT-IN per discipline: rules_electrical.json carries no such key and runs the legacy blob path byte-identically (proven on its 2,888-row labelled corpus).

decay._note: HVAC proximity-decay curve, wired EXPLICITLY at HV-3 (2026-07-20) rather than left to the implicit flat default, so the value is a measured decision on the record. MEASURED FLAT: the tracked decay_sweep.py harness was run over the 1366 labelled Set-1 line items (the same row set as SCORING_V0.md) across the certified 20-value ladder. Flat m=1.0 scored 52.86% and NO multiplier beat it -- best non-flat was m=0.90 at 52.27% (-8 rows); m<=0.75 fell to ~49.4%. This mirrors the Electrical result (D2/D2b), where decay was also measured and LOCKED FLAT. PROVISIONAL-FIT: fitted on the team's PROVISIONAL Set-1 labels (labels carrying known vocabulary drift and an unfinished preamble pass); a re-sweep is OWED once clean labels land, and this value must not be treated as certified until then. Electrical's locked 1.0 is a separate, untouched decision -- rules_electrical.json deliberately carries no decay block.

rules.plain: Names sheet-metal ductwork (GI/GSS, spiral/oval/round) fabricated + installed by gauge/area.
Sits under a Ducting section header.
An air-distribution product: grille/diffuser/damper (incl. fire damper)/VCD/louver/spigot/collar.
A plenum box is an air-distribution product (not an electrical/control panel).
R1: a flexible / aluminium-foil duct is an air-distribution PRODUCT, not fabricated ductwork. Ducting means rigid sheet-metal work made to gauge; a flex duct is bought as an accessory.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance ADP rate sheet

rules.plain: R1 (ancestor form): size leaves under a flexible/foil duct header inherit ADP.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance ADP rate sheet

rules.plain: R1 guard (line): Ducting NEVER scores in a flexible/foil duct context -- Ducting is rigid fabricated sheet-metal only.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance ADP rate sheet

rules.plain: R1 guard (ancestor): children of a flexible/foil duct header can never be Ducting either.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance ADP rate sheet

rules.plain: R6: a canvas / flexible connection resolves by SERVED CONTEXT. The rule grammar has no conditional, so the ruling is expressed as a WEIGHT WINDOW: with the 0.05 direct-signal ranking bonus this scores 0.47 effective, which clears the duct-section ancestor (DUCT-ANC 0.45 -> ADP wins under a duct/air-distribution header) but stays under the fan-section ancestor (FAN-ANC-TYPE 0.5 -> Fans wins under a fan header). CAUTION: that window is only 0.03 wide (0.40 < w < 0.45); any future change to DUCT-ANC, FAN-ANC-TYPE or scoring.direct_signal_bonus will silently break this ruling. It is covered both directions by tests.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance ADP / Fans rate sheets

rules.plain: R5: damper ACCESSORIES price with the damper package. A child of a damper header -- actuator, fire sensor, MFD/damper control panel -- is ADP.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance ADP / Dampers rate sheet

rules.plain: R3: a plenum is an air-distribution product. At 0.5 this outranks AHU-ANC (0.45) at the same resolution point, so 'SUPPLY AIR PLENUMS FOR AHUs' resolves to ADP, not AHU.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance ADP rate sheet

rules.plain: Sits under a grille/diffuser (air distribution) section. HV-3 KEEPS this token and its 0.4 weight, both on measured evidence. Hypothesis H2 proposed DELETING 'air distribution' as over-broad; the Set-1 labels REVERSED that -- truth agreed with ADP on 84% of the 223 rows the token decides -- so the token stays. Raising the weight was then measured and REJECTED: at 0.45 or 0.5 the rule outranks (or ties and wins the tiebreak against) the sibling 0.45 ancestors DUCT-ANC / AHU-ANC / VRF-ANC, and overall accuracy falls 52.86% -> 50.29% on the same 1366 rows (45 ducting, 31 AHU and 23 VRF rows lost to ADP). H2's 84% was measured on rows ADP ALREADY won; amplifying the weight extends the rule into a different population where truth says ducting/AHU/VRF. Correct reading: keep the signal, do not amplify it.
HVAC piping: chilled/condenser water, copper refrigerant, or drain pipe.

Sits under a Piping section header. M2 (HV-5): the SINGULAR 'pipe' tokens were added -- real headers say 'DRAIN PIPE' and 'REFRIGERANT PIPE', which the plural-only token missed, so pure pipe-size leaves inherited Insulation or VRF instead of Piping. This is hypothesis H5, deferred since HV-3 and settled here by the deep-dive trace evidence.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance Piping rate sheet

rules.plain: Duct/pipe thermal or acoustic insulation (nitrile/elastomeric/fiberglass/cladding).
Sits under an Insulation section header.

OWNER RULING (the 4A convention, HV-3): when an insulation word appears as an ATTRIBUTE of a pipe or valve line -- 'insulated pipe', 'pipe with insulation', 'insulated butterfly valve', a composite '5/8 dia with 13 mm insulation' -- the line is priced as the pipe or the valve, NOT as Insulation. Insulation claims a row only when insulation is the SUBJECT of the line (a standalone insulation item or an Insulation section). Encodes hypothesis H4, which the Set-1 labels CONFIRMED at 100% on its 66-row pile.

A valve or valve-assembly line (butterfly/NRV/balancing/PICV/strainer). A valve itemised INSIDE a CHW/AHU unit package may instead belong to that unit -- kept MED, not HIGH, without a Valves-section ancestor.
Sits under a Valves section header.

Sits under a preamble that names a SPECIFIC valve type. HV-4 mined: valve size leaves were losing a three-way 0.40 tie (insulation / valve / chilled-water) at the SAME ancestor, because a valve specification paragraph incidentally mentions insulation and chilled water; an explicit valve-type header outranks those incidental mentions. Reopens hypothesis H3 (deferred at HV-3) under the nearest-hit regime, where its pile is genuinely different. KNOWN COST: valves itemised INSIDE an AHU / CHW unit package (9 rows on Set-1) are pulled to Valve Package -- the contested boundary VLV-KW's own plain already flags; kept because the trade is 127 rows won for 9 lost (14.1x).

R2: pipeline instruments -- BTU / energy / flow meters, thermometers, thermowells, pressure and temperature gauges, test points -- price with the VALVE PACKAGE (the pipe-fitting supplier), not with Sensors. PROMOTED FROM PROVISIONAL: HV-3 shipped this at weight 0.2 pending evidence because H7 had proposed Sensors and the labels refuted it; the owner's workbook now settles it, so it carries full keyword weight.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance Valve Package rate sheet

rules.plain: R2 (ancestor form): size leaves under an instrument header ('Ultrasonic BTU meters') inherit Valve Package. This also makes the instrument preamble an INFORMATIVE resolution point, so the walk stops there instead of continuing out to the enclosing section.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance Valve Package rate sheet

rules.plain: A VAV/CAV terminal box (CFM-rated air terminal).
Sits under a VAV section header.
A sensor, transmitter, thermostat, or BMS/BACnet controller / integration item.
Sits under a Sensors / Controls / BMS section header.
A ventilation/exhaust/axial/inline fan, kitchen exhaust, scrubber, or make-up air unit (NOT an FCU fan coil or an AHU plug fan).
Sits under a Ventilation / Fans section header.

Sits under a preamble naming a SPECIFIC fan type. HV-4 mined: bare CFM-capacity leaves under an inline / fresh-air fan header were inheriting ducting, because the fan spec mentions duct connections. NARROWED BY THE MINING FLOOR: the batch was proposed with nine tokens and measured at 75.0% precision -- below the 85% floor -- so every token was scored individually and only these two cleared it (inline fan 97.2%/5 BoQs, fresh air fan 97.3%/5 BoQs). 'exhaust air' (53.3%), 'ventilation unit'/'ventilation units' (0%) and 'centrifugal fan' (single BoQ) were REJECTED by the floor.
A chilled-water terminal unit (FCU / fan coil / CSU / chilled-water unit).

CHW/DX boundary law (HV-6): cassette / hi-wall / ductable is a FORM FACTOR, not a category. It resolves to CHW only together with a WATER-FED context -- from the line's own text or its section header (CHW-ANC). Bare form with neither context stays weak and contested on purpose: do not guess.
CHW/DX boundary law (HV-6): sits under a Chilled Water / FCU / water-fed section header. The FEED MEDIUM decides the category, not the form factor.
A direct-expansion split unit / condensing unit (non-VRF).

CHW/DX boundary law (HV-6): sits under a DX / condensing-unit section header. Mirrors CHW-ANC (0.4) so the FEED MEDIUM decides from section context too, regardless of form factor. The bare word 'refrigerant' is deliberately NOT a token here: VRF is refrigerant-fed as well, and VRF keeps precedence (see DX-VRF-EXCL).

CHW/DX boundary law (HV-6): cassette / hi-wall / split is a FORM FACTOR, not a category. It resolves to DX only together with a REFRIGERANT-FED context -- from the line's own text or its section header (DX-ANC). Bare form with neither context stays weak and contested on purpose: do not guess.
A VRF/VRV system unit (ODU/IDU). Owner rule: a cabling line between ODU and IDU is hvac_cables, so a VRF line naming cabling yields the category to Cables (excluded here).
A VRF ancillary: refnet/Y-joint, refrigerant gas topping, or ODU stand. NOTE: VRF control CABLING is hvac_cables, not here.

VRF controllers ruling (HV-6): a VRF/VRV system's OWN controls -- corded / wireless remote, centralised remote controller, intelligent touch manager -- price with the VRF package. Sensors keeps the BMS basket only (BACnet/BMS integration controllers, transmitters, thermostats); see SNS-VRFCTRL-EXCL for the other direction.
Sits under a VRF section header.

HVAC power/control cabling or wiring. OWNS VRF control cabling (VRF keeps only refnet/gas/stand ancillaries). HV-3: the tray tokens ('cable tray', 'perforated tray') moved OUT to hvac_raceway on the owner's raceway ruling -- Cables is cabling only.
Sits under a Cabling section header. HV-3: 'cable tray' moved OUT to RCW-ANC.

RACEWAY CARVE-OUT guard (HV-3, owner ruling), Cables side: a tray/raceway line contains the word 'cable', so without this guard CBL-KW would claim every cable tray. A line naming a tray or raceway is hvac_raceway, never hvac_cables.
A cable tray / raceway / tray accessory. HV-3 owner ruling: trays and raceways are a separately-priced package, not part of Cables (which is cabling only).
Sits under a Cable Tray / Raceway section header. Weight mirrors electrical's equivalent tray ancestor rule (CT-ANC, 0.4) -- the same signal in the sibling discipline.
RACEWAY CARVE-OUT guard (HV-3), Raceway side: a unit's drip/drain/condensate tray is part of that unit, not a cable-carrying raceway. Keeps the new category from stealing DX/CHW/VRF unit accessories.
An air handling unit / TFA unit / cooling coil / AHU accessory (incl. the AHU plug fan).
Sits under an AHU section header.
A starter/control/VFD panel for HVAC equipment (NOT a double-skin AHU/plenum casing panel).

R3 guard: when the resolution point is a PLENUM header, AHU is forbidden for its children even though the header names the AHUs the plenums serve. The plenum is the product; the AHU is only its destination.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance ADP rate sheet

rules.plain: R4 guard: when the resolution point is a PANEL header, AHU is forbidden for its children. 'AHU STARTER PANEL' is a panel that serves an AHU, not an AHU.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance Panels rate sheet

rules.plain: R5 guard (Panels side): a control panel under a DAMPER header is part of the damper package (ADP). Generic panels outside damper context are untouched -- this fires only at a damper resolution point.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance ADP / Dampers rate sheet

rules.plain: R5 guard (Sensors side): actuators and fire sensors under a DAMPER header belong to the damper package. BMS-context sensors are untouched -- this fires only at a damper resolution point.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance ADP / Dampers rate sheet

rules.plain: R9 guard: an FCU quoted 'along with factory fitted valve package' stays CHW Units -- the composite prices with the unit. Without this the HV-4 valve-header rule pulls the FCU capacity leaves to Valve Package.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance CHW Units / FCU rate sheet

rules.plain: M1 -- the owner's 4A composite ruling lifted from the line to the ANCESTOR. When a section header describes a HOST item (pipe / duct / valve) and mentions insulation only as an attribute of it ('MS chilled water pipes shall be insulated with nitrile rubber insulation'), its children price as the HOST, never as Insulation. The pattern requires at least TWO intervening words between the host noun and the insulation word, which is what separates the attribute form from the compound-noun item form: 'duct insulation', 'pipe insulation' and 'underdeck insulation' are adjacent and therefore NEVER match, so the three 4A insulation-is-the-item families still win.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance Insulation rate sheet

rules.plain: R4: a panel section header places Panels at 0.5, outranking AHU-ANC (0.45) at the same resolution point.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance Panels rate sheet

rules.plain: Sits under a Panels section header.
A CHW primary/secondary/condenser pump set (NOT a unit drain pump nor a VRF heat pump).
Sits under a Pumps section header.

A standalone HVAC service/hardware line: T&B/commissioning, water treatment, vibration isolators, dismantling/recommissioning. A positive read for genuine HVAC misc, NOT a fallback for uncertainty (that stays blank).

R10 (owner redraw 2026-07-21) at weight 0.6, ABOVE the item-keyword band (0.55) on purpose: a work line must outrank the system noun it names, or 'Dismantling of existing ducting' scores Ducting. WORK / SERVICE lines -- recommissioning, tapping, dismantling, modification, re-routing, associated civil chipping/chasing -- join T&B and commissioning in Misc REGARDLESS of the system they touch. A tapping into a chilled-water line is service work, not Piping. GUARDED by exclude_if: where those verbs appear inside a supply-and-install scope (an SITC line), the ITEM still wins and this rule stands down.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance Misc / Services rate sheet

rules.plain: R7: a STANDALONE filter item (MERV/HEPA/pre-filter, incl. temporary construction-phase filters) is Misc. Filters INTEGRAL to a fan/AHU/unit line stay with that unit -- that half of the ruling is carried by AHU-FILTER-EXCL below, not by this rule.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance Misc rate sheet

rules.plain: R7 guard: a line whose SUBJECT is the filter ('MERV 13 Filters for AHUs', 'temporary filters for Air Handling Units') is a standalone filter item, so AHU is forbidden and Misc wins. A genuine AHU line that merely lists its filters among its parts does not match these patterns and keeps AHU.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance Misc rate sheet

rules.plain: R8: air curtains are Misc, not Fans.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance Misc rate sheet

rules.plain: R8 guard: an air-curtain line names a fan in its specification, so Fans is forbidden outright.
rules.source: owner ruling 2026-07-21, workbook provenance Misc rate sheet

rules.plain: CHW/DX boundary law (HV-6), VRF precedence: VRF/VRV systems are refrigerant-fed too, so a RESOLUTION POINT naming VRF/VRV forbids DX for its children -- DX means NON-VRF direct expansion. Ancestor-scoped (HV-5 mechanism) because the form-factor leaf itself rarely repeats the system name.

VRF controllers ruling (HV-6), other direction: a VRF remote / central controller is NOT a BMS sensor, so Sensors is forbidden on those lines. Sensors keeps BACnet/BMS integration controllers, transmitters and thermostats.
